title: Connection Shepherd: abort signaling and partial-result summaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: long-running streaming generations can be left in limbo after abrupt client disconnects, causing KV cache leaks, orphaned GPU work, and noisy billing. Existing GC thresholds are static and often either reclaim too aggressively (losing resumability) or too conservatively (wasting resources).

Goal: introduce a lightweight Connection Shepherd process that tracks per-generation liveness using a combination of client signals and telemetry-derived heuristics, provide a deterministic abort/finalize handshake, and emit compact partial-result summaries for customers and downstream tooling. The feature must preserve resumability when appropriate, offer a configurable eviction grace credit, and expose observability for tuning GC thresholds.
design_decisions: Create ephemeral Connection Shepherd actor that attaches metadata to generation metadata rather than replacing existing lease code
Use three-level abort fence: soft-warning (retain resumability), hard-abort (free KV/gpu state), and finalizer (emit partial summary and tombstone), controlled by telemetry buckets
Introduce 'grace credits' per connection which are consumed on transient disconnects; credits replenish on successful reconnect or after admin policy window
Partial-result summary format: compact JSON with token-range, deterministic checksum, function-call events, and confidence statistics — designed for Console and customer webhooks
Expose tuning knobs via route-level config: grace_window_ms, grace_credits, telemetry_bucket_thresholds, finalizer_timeout_ms
acceptance_criteria: Connection Shepherd can attach/detach to a streaming generation without requiring schema changes to existing runtime metadata

Default policy reclaims >90% of orphaned GPU allocations within configured finalizer_timeout while preserving resumability for transient disconnects in at least 95% of reconnect cases within grace_window
Partial-result summaries emitted to Console and customer webhooks when finalizer runs; samples available in debugging dashboard

New telemetry metrics (shepherd_attach, shepherd_soft_warn, shepherd_hard_abort, partial_summary_emitted) are ingested into the runtime metrics pipeline and visualized on the streaming-reliability dashboard
E2E tests covering client abrupt disconnect, network partition, and reconnect scenarios with assertions on resource cleanup and resumability
Security review completed for any metadata fields sent to external webhooks (marked safe/no-PII)
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Spike completed. Observed three common disconnect patterns: immediate client close, long idle then close, and intermittent socket flapping. Sketching shepherd actor API.
2026-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented PoC shepherd and a mock finalizer. PoC reclaims GPU state reliably in staging; need to tune grace credits after load test.
2026-03-05 - Design review (J. Ramos): prefer compact summary to avoid storing full token traces. Agreed to include deterministic checksum and token_range metadata.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2028 - initial shepherd runtime + unit tests

2026-03-09 - Perf test: under sustained 10k concurrent streams, default finalizer_timeout_ms=45000 reclaimed 87% of orphans within window. Plan: add telemetry-driven bucket to shorten timeouts for churny clients.

2026-03-11 - QA: Added E2E reconnect test that validates resumability when reconnect happens within grace_window (passing). Found race where function-call side-effects could be double-invoked — created follow-up task ENG-648301.
notes: Compatibility: The shepherd is designed as a compatibility layer and will not change the external API surface. Existing SDKs will continue to see the same streaming events unless finalizer emits a partial summary artifact.
Billing: when hard-abort triggers, billing stops for the generation. We must coordinate with billing infra to ensure true-up for partial generations is handled consistently.
Migration path: roll out as opt-in per-route flag; gather telemetry for 2 weeks; then consider default-on for routes with >5% orphan rate.
Follow-ups: ENG-648301 (function-call dedupe), PM-4091 (console UX for partial summaries), ENG-648305 (billing integration testing)
